findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how Tier-1 guarantees the verifier `context` matches production: reconstruct byte-exact plan text from EDIT history where intact (as celestine-treasonous-ewe already does) and only fall back to normalized-equivalent text with the residual difference recorded — OR scope out Pass-2 questions sensitive to the normalized-away/excluded basis (checkbox state, whitespace, title) — rather than asserting normalized-basis equivalence suffices.
evidence: Plan: 'Re-run the verifier with candidate questions/prompt on the stored Pass-1 findings plus reconstructed plan text … normalized-basis equivalence is what the replay needs, not byte-exact text.'
The verifier's `context` is the full plan text including AC checkboxes/headings — tests/external/test_review_kernel_rules_live.py:48 (`_PLAN_CONTEXT` carries `## Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] …`).

The fingerprint normalizes exactly this away: tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py + tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1181 (checkbox-flip invariance) and material_diff excludes title/description_boxes from the basis.
The plan asserts the equivalence is 'what the replay needs' without establishing that stored Pass-2 answers are insensitive to the normalized-away/excluded basis (checkbox state, whitespace, title).
The child ticket celestine-treasonous-ewe already replays EDIT history (byte-exact where intact), so higher-fidelity `context` is often recoverable — the epic-level Tier-1 framing under-uses it.
findings.finding: Tier-1 assumes fingerprint-equivalent reconstructed material is an adequate substitute for the plan text the Pass-2 verifier actually reads, but the verifier consumes the full plan as free-text `context` (incl. AC checkbox state, whitespace, and title) while the material fingerprint normalizes checkbox-state/whitespace away and excludes the title — so a fingerprint match does not establish `context`-text equivalence for questions sensitive to those elements.
findings.location: Approach → Tier 1 ("reconstructed plan text via the verify_findings(run_chunk=…) seam"; "normalized-basis equivalence is what the replay needs, not byte-exact text") and AC #4
scenarios: A candidate Pass-2 question keys on whether an AC's test-coverage checkbox is checked; the reconstructed context has checkbox state normalized, so the replayed answer diverges from the stored one for reasons unrelated to the question change.

A stored finding/answer references the plan title (excluded from the fingerprint basis); the reconstructed context restores a different or absent title, corrupting the per-question agreement score that AC #4 uses to establish the noise floor.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope/repair AC #8 and the Tier-2 cost model against the MEASURED Opus-on-Bedrock silent-caching failure (ADR 0059 §7 / Correction #10): either (a) route a cheap live cache-probe SPIKE on the exact configured frontier id (bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8) before committing Tier-2 spend, and (b) if Opus does not cache, restate AC #8 to the passes/models that demonstrably cache (Sonnet/Pass-2) and re-estimate Tier-2 at full-input-billed-every-call.
evidence: Plan AC: 'Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call); verified from the usage log.'
Plan Tier 2: 'Re-run finders … Opus, ~$3.4/review uncached'; Invariant 2: 'frontier Opus for Pass 1 … through Bedrock only … Substituting a cheaper model to save budget is forbidden.'

docs/adr/0059-llm-provider-seam-and-support-tiers.md §7: 'us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-… AND global.anthropic.… both returned cache_read=0 and cache_write=0 on both attempts with the full 4029 input tokens billed every call — no error, no warning. … This silent double-billing is the real hazard.'
docs/adr/0059 Correction #10: 'Bedrock does not straightforwardly fix the opus caching failure … The opus-4-5 datapoint is never reconciled (§7).'
tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py:10-14 — the live cache canary asserts cache_read_tokens>0 only on the DEFAULT model us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6, not on any Opus profile.
A prior cached plan-review comment (.rebar/cache/plan-review/759e-…/9d0c…json) raised: 'Reconcile AC #8 with the measured Opus-on-Bedrock caching failure.'
findings.finding: AC #8 ('prompt caching confirmed active for eval runs, cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call') and the Tier-2 cost model (~$3.4/review on Opus) assume prompt caching works on Opus-via-Bedrock, but the codebase records a MEASURED, UNRECONCILED silent caching failure for the Opus family on Bedrock: ADR 0059 §7 states us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-… (and global.) returned cache_read=0/cache_write=0 with the full input billed every call, and Correction #10 says 'the opus-4-5 datapoint is never reconciled'. The positive Bedrock caching evidence and the only live cache canary (tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py) cover SONNET only. Since Invariant 2 forbids substituting a cheaper model and pins Pass-1 to frontier Opus on Bedrock, whether AC #8 is even satisfiable for the Pass-1 pass — and whether the ~$3.4/review estimate holds under full-input-billed-every-call — is unverified/contradicted for the configured frontier id bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8.
findings.location: Approach → Tier 2 (~$3.4/review); Invariant 2 (Model parity); Acceptance Criteria: prompt-caching AC (#8)
scenarios: Commissioning a Tier-2 baseline run on Opus-via-Bedrock: cache_read_tokens stays 0 on every call, so AC #8's verification never passes AND every uncached call is billed at full input — blowing the per-review estimate and eating into the $200 cap far faster than planned.
The harness's own cache-zero guard (structured_run warn_if_cache_ineffective) fires on the Opus pass, which the plan treats as a blocking anomaly, stalling Tier-2 commissioning.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Tier-2 pre-commissioning SPIKE: run tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py's canary against bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8; if it returns cache_read_tokens==0, (1) scope AC #8's 'caching confirmed active' to the Sonnet Pass-2 runs, (2) recompute the Tier-2 per-review cost with no cache credit, and (3) publish the resulting Opus-uncached per-proposal cost so the $200/$120 budgets reflect it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the eval runner's behavior when a Bedrock call fails mid-run: either disable the production fallback chain for eval runs (Bedrock-only, fail loud on error) or reject any result whose recorded per-pass model id is not the expected Bedrock production id, so an in-run fallover cannot silently break parity/caching or the budget cap.
evidence: Invariant #2: 'through Bedrock only, on a homogeneous provider chain (mixed Bedrock+Anthropic silently disables prompt caching and roughly doubles cost)'.

Invariant #2's enforcement is start-time only: 'refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's provider_provenance.ran_model' — no clause covers an in-run Bedrock failure.

src/rebar/llm/runner.py has an active fallback chain (fallback_targets_for, build_fallback_model, entered_fallback_model) that engages on a call failure; the plan never states the eval runner disables it.

AC: 'Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call)' — a mid-run fallover to Anthropic would zero this and roughly double spend against the $200 cap, undetected because the failed sub-step's fallback is unspecified.
findings.finding: The harness enforces Bedrock-only model parity only as a PRE-FLIGHT check (refuse to start when the configured model differs from the baseline), but specifies no fallback behavior for a Bedrock call that FAILS mid-run during a Tier-1/Tier-2 eval — leaving the production runner's active fallback chain free to silently substitute a non-production/non-Bedrock model, violating invariant #2 and the AC-8 caching guarantee.
findings.location: Approach → invariant #2 (Model parity); Acceptance Criteria lines on model-id refusal and prompt caching
scenarios: A Tier-1 (Sonnet) or Tier-2 (Opus) run hits a transient Bedrock error partway through the stratified sample; the runner's configured fallback chain fails over to Anthropic, disabling prompt caching and roughly doubling cost while still passing the start-time parity gate.
The resulting eval result carries a per-pass model id from a non-Bedrock provider, contaminating a diff or a published per-proposal cost figure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to invariant #2 that eval runs disable the runner's fallback chain (no_chain / empty fallback_targets) and fail loud on a Bedrock error, AND that the model-id parity check is re-asserted post-call against every result's recorded per-pass model id (not only at pre-flight), refusing to record or diff any result whose ran_model is not the expected Bedrock production id.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reorder the decomposition so the ledger (4c80) and parity/Bedrock guard (efd4) land before the Tier-1 (53ab) and Tier-2 (f1d6) harnesses, or add explicit depends_on edges from 53ab/f1d6 to 4c80 and efd4.
evidence: Parent decomposition: 'Corpus (1) -> labels/noise floor (2) -> Tier-0 (3) -> Tier-1 (4) -> Tier-2 (5) -> ledger + model-parity + Bedrock chain (6-8 ...)'
Child 53ab Approach: 'All calls go through the budget ledger pre-flight (estimate = stored metrics tokens x current price x N) and record the model id per result.'
Child 53ab body: candidate verifier run 'through the production PydanticAIRunner pinned to the standard class on Bedrock' — i.e. relies on the parity guard's pinning.

Child f1d6 Approach: 'Budget pre-flight from stored per-criterion usage ... x current price' and 'a run is refused when the frontier model is not the Bedrock Opus id' — both depend on ledger + parity.
Child efd4 (parity guard) and 4c80 (ledger) are the position 6-8 items the tier harnesses consume.
findings.finding: The parent's stated build order sequences the budget ledger and model-parity/Bedrock guard (decomposition positions 6-8) AFTER the Tier-1 (position 4) and Tier-2 (position 5) harnesses, yet both tier harnesses structurally require the ledger pre-flight and the parity guard to already exist before they can run any LLM call.
findings.location: child 53ab-bdf6-de1c-4bb1 (Tier-1) and child f1d6-cfcc-a9c6-416d (Tier-2); parent 'Child decomposition' ordering
scenarios: Tier-1 commissioning run (53ab, position 4) is built and executed before the ledger (4c80) exists, so its ~$40 spend is not pre-flighted or recorded against the $200 cap.
Tier-2 baseline run (f1d6) executes on a mixed Bedrock+Anthropic chain because the parity guard (efd4) that would pin/refuse has not been wired in yet, silently disabling caching and ~2x-ing cost.
findings.suggested_fix: State build order corpus->labels->ledger+parity->tier0->tier1->tier2->protocol, and add depends_on from Tier-1 and Tier-2 to both the ledger and the parity-guard children.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit depends_on from the ledger (4c80) to the usage_log fix (860f), or confirm the ledger's per-run file attribution does not rely on the usage row ticket id.
evidence: Child 4c80 Context: 'The eval ledger needs per-run attribution and this is the cheapest fix on that path.' (referring to the usage_log bug)
Child 4c80 Approach: 'every eval run opens a usage-log session with REBAR_USAGE_LOG pointed at a per-run file; on completion the rows are priced and the ledger row finalised'
Child 860f: '0 of the ~11,900 rows in .rebar/usage.jsonl carry a ticket ... per-ticket (and therefore per-review) cost attribution from the usage log is impossible'
Parent decomposition lumps '(6-8, incl. the usage-log bug)' but states no ordering between the ledger and the fix.
findings.finding: The eval budget ledger (4c80) depends on the usage_log ticket-attribution fix (860f) for per-run/per-ticket attribution, but neither child declares an ordering dependency between them; 4c80's metering opens a usage-log session and prices rows, and without 860f those rows carry no ticket id.
scenarios: 4c80 lands and commissioning runs are metered before 860f lands; ledger rows/detail rows cannot be attributed to the reviewed ticket, weakening the ledger's per-run attribution that AC6 relies on.
findings.suggested_fix: Sequence 860f before 4c80 (or before the first commissioning run) and note the dependency in both children.
